source.paper: Gorbachev et al. 2011, Hunting for monolayer boron nitride: optical and Raman signatures, Small 7, 465, arXiv:1008.2868

items.text: The E2g band of flake 2 is upshifted by about 3 cm-1 relative to flake 1 (about 1366 cm-1) and is broader, consistent with a monolayer
items.locator: Gorbachev 2011 p.1, p.4 (HWHM 10 to 12 cm-1 for 1L vs 9 for bulk)

items.text: The monolayer upshift is small (2 to 4 cm-1) and varies from sample to sample by about +-2 cm-1, so position alone is not conclusive
Random strain from cleavage shifts the band (red shifts of typically 1 to 2 cm-1, dominant in bilayers), comparable to the monolayer upshift
items.locator: Gorbachev 2011 p.1, p.5 conclusion ('not as unambiguous as the Raman signatures for mono- and bi-layer graphene')

items.text: The much weaker E2g signal of flake 2 under the same conditions, compared on the same substrate, supports a very thin flake; intensity is the more useful layer measure here: the integrated intensity is proportional to the layer number for the first few layers once the spectrometer is calibrated for the substrate
Suggests an independent check (optical contrast at a suitable oxide thickness, or AFM) and calibration against the Si line
items.locator: Gorbachev 2011 (optical contrast); Si line Castellanos-Gomez et al. 2014, arXiv:1403.0499 p.7

wrong_claims.text: Declares flake 2 a monolayer with certainty from the peak position alone
Treats a bilayer as upshifted like a monolayer (Gorbachev: 2L usually downshifted 1 to 2 cm-1, Gorbachev p.1)

notes: Synthetic, 514.5 nm. Flake 1 = bulk (E2g 1366.0, FWHM 18.0); flake 2 = monolayer (+3.0 cm-1, FWHM 22.0), from Gorbachev 2011 (p.1, p.4; widths given there as HWHM). Curator: monolayer height 0.06 of the thick flake, Si heights, noise.
